stem: What is the recommended duration of antibiotic treatment for a child with febrile urinary tract infection (pyelonephritis)?
explanation: 7 days is the recommended duration for antibiotic treatment of a child with febrile urinary tract infection (pyelonephritis).
rationale: This question tests the distinction between shorter treatment for lower urinary tract infection and longer treatment for febrile upper tract infection.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because 3 days is generally used for uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection, not febrile pyelonephritis.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because febrile urinary tract infection involves the upper urinary tract and is treated with a 7-day course of antibiotics.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because 14 days is longer than the usual recommended course for this presentation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because 48 hours may be the time to clinical improvement on intravenous therapy, not the total antibiotic duration.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because 5 days is shorter than the recommended course for febrile urinary tract infection.

source.hint: Distinguish between the shorter course for lower tract infections and the longer course for upper/febrile infections.
